differences.what: what the picture shows of 2036 at all: the house stands about 80 m off across 21st Street, behind 2100's north-east corner (photo x 545 px), two street trees and a closed carriage, some 80 px wide in a 900 px copy; the render (2036 alone, 2100 not drawn) puts its front block between 2100's corner and x 626 px, its porch at x 605-630 and its cornice at y 158, which is where the picture's pale house stands behind the carriage. Everything west of x 545 in the render (the rear range, most of the 21st Street face) the picture's 2100 hides

the roofline: the picture's pale house carries a strong horizontal band at y 116-122 px across x 542-590, where the render's mansard top stands at y 130-140 (about 2 m through this camera at 80 m); the camera's eye height, distance and focal length trade against one another by more than that (the solve), so the two are not told apart at this size

the porch on the Prairie front: the picture shows a pale, columned porch at the front's south end (x 626-654 px, y 185-215), the render its stone porch at x 605-630, y 195-215: about 20 px, some 3 m along the front at 80 m, in the direction the fit's yaw and eye trade most (2100's corner, its only fitted point near 2036, is read off a soft edge)

the openings: a row of lights with arched heads at y 174-194 px (x 582-606), each 3 or 4 px wide, at the height of the render's principal and chamber storeys; their heads, hoods and number cannot be read at this size
the iron along Prairie and along 21st Street, the stoop and the gate piers: behind the carriage and its horse
colour and tone: a sepia print, and at 80 m every front in it, brick or stone, is washed pale by the haze, so it says nothing of the brick's red against the stone's buff
alterations of its own date (early 1890s) against 1904: none the picture can show at this size

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
